prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The present invention relates to fluid dispensing devices for use in dispensing different liquids (e.g., bleach and bleach activator) from a bottle having first and second compartments. To minimize the presence of mixed composition residually present within the fluid dispensing device, it may be helpful to delay mixing. Separate dip tubes may be provided to pull liquid from the separate compartments, each with its own separate pump. Each pump may deliver the separate compositions to a spray nozzle of the device through separate delivery tubes (e.g., from the pumps to the nozzle). In other embodiments, a single delivery tube, and/or a single pump may be provided, e.g., where the volume of mixed composition that may be present in such pump and/or delivery tube may be sufficiently small so as to still provide overall desired efficacy characteristics. Dual delivery tube configurations may eliminate any need to prime the device by spraying out old, residual mixed composition.

outputs.L1: The present invention relates to fluid dispensing devices for dispensing different liquids (e.g., bleach and bleach activator) from a bottle having first and second compartments. To minimize the residual presence of a mixed composition within the fluid dispensing device, it may be desirable to delay mixing. Separate dip tubes may be provided to draw liquid from the respective compartments, with each dip tube associated with its own separate pump. Each pump may deliver the separate compositions to a spray nozzle of the device through separate delivery tubes (e.g., extending from the pumps to the nozzle). In other embodiments, a single delivery tube and/or a single pump may be provided, e.g., where the volume of mixed composition that may be present in such pump and/or delivery tube is sufficiently small to still provide the desired overall efficacy characteristics. Dual delivery tube configurations may eliminate any need to prime the device by spraying out old, residual mixed composition.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns liquid-dispensing apparatuses designed to dispense multiple fluids, such as bleach and a bleach activator, from a container that includes two separate chambers. To reduce the amount of blended material left behind inside the dispensing mechanism, it can be advantageous to postpone mixing until later in the flow path. In some configurations, individual dip tubes draw liquid from the respective chambers, with each liquid being moved by its own pump. These pumps may then send the separate formulations to the device’s spray nozzle through independent delivery conduits, such as tubes extending from the pumps to the nozzle. In other versions, the device may use only one delivery tube and/or a single pump, for example when the quantity of mixed formulation remaining in that pump or tube is small enough that the desired performance of the product is still maintained. Arrangements using two delivery tubes may remove the need to prime the dispenser by spraying out previously mixed residual composition.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to fluid dispensing devices configured to dispense two different liquids from a bottle having two separate compartments. Each compartment may contain a different liquid component, and the dispensing device is arranged to draw the liquids from their respective compartments and dispense them together, for example through a spray nozzle.

In certain applications, it is desirable to keep the liquids separated until shortly before dispensing. Delaying the mixing of the liquids can help reduce the amount of mixed composition that remains inside the dispenser after use. This may be important where the mixed composition has reduced stability, loses effectiveness over time, or may otherwise be undesirable if left in the internal passages of the dispensing mechanism between uses.

In some embodiments, the dispenser includes separate dip tubes and separate pumps. Each dip tube extends into a respective compartment of the bottle and draws liquid from that compartment. Each pump then moves its corresponding liquid through a separate flow path toward the spray nozzle. The liquids may remain separated through most of the dispensing system and may be combined only near the nozzle, at the nozzle, or immediately after discharge. This arrangement can minimize the volume of residual mixed composition remaining inside the device.

Other embodiments may use a single pump or a shared delivery tube for at least part of the flow path. Such configurations may be suitable where the amount of residual mixed composition left inside the dispenser is sufficiently small that it does not materially affect the desired performance or efficacy of the dispensed product. In these embodiments, the design may balance simplicity, cost, manufacturability, and performance while still limiting the drawbacks associated with residual mixed liquid.

Dual delivery tube configurations may also reduce or eliminate the need to prime the device before use. In conventional systems where mixed composition remains in the dispenser, a user may need to spray one or more times to clear old residual mixture before applying a fresh composition. By keeping the liquids separate until they are dispensed, a dual delivery tube arrangement can ensure that the composition delivered during each use is fresh and effective, thereby avoiding waste and improving user convenience.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a dispensing device for storing and dispensing two or more liquid compositions that are intended to remain separated until the time of use. In conventional multi-compartment dispensing bottles, different liquids may be drawn from separate reservoirs but can become mixed within shared internal passages, such as a common dip tube, pump chamber, outlet channel, or nozzle. After dispensing stops, a portion of the mixed liquid may remain trapped in these shared passages. This residual mixed composition can create several disadvantages, including product waste, reduced effectiveness of active ingredients, instability of the formulation, clogging, discoloration, odor formation, or the need to prime the dispenser before the next use in order to clear the previously mixed material.

The present invention addresses these problems by providing a multi-compartment dispensing system in which each liquid is kept substantially separate throughout most or all of the flow path inside the dispensing device. In one embodiment, the bottle includes a plurality of compartments, each containing a different liquid component. Each compartment is connected to its own dip tube, pump mechanism, and delivery tube, so that the liquids are not combined inside the bottle or pump assembly. The separate liquid streams are instead brought together only at or near the dispensing outlet, such as at the nozzle, spray orifice, applicator tip, or immediately outside the dispenser during use.

In another embodiment, the device may include some shared structure, but any shared portion of the flow path is minimized in volume and length. For example, separate dip tubes and pump chambers may feed into a short common outlet passage located very close to the dispensing opening. By reducing the internal volume where the liquids can mix, the amount of mixed composition remaining in the dispenser after actuation is greatly reduced. In some configurations, the shared passage may be so small that substantially no meaningful quantity of mixed product remains after dispensing.

The invention may be used with a wide variety of products in which separate storage and delayed mixing are desirable. Examples include cleaning compositions, disinfectants, hair colorants, cosmetic treatments, skin-care products, adhesives, foaming systems, reactive chemical formulations, food or beverage additives, pharmaceutical preparations, and other products containing ingredients that may lose potency, react prematurely, separate, degrade, or otherwise become less desirable if mixed too early.

By delaying the mixing of the different liquids until the moment of dispensing, the device helps preserve the intended properties and efficacy of the final composition. It also reduces or eliminates the need for a user to prime the dispenser to remove leftover mixed material from a previous use. As a result, the dispenser can provide a more consistent product composition from one use to the next, reduce waste, improve shelf life, and enhance overall reliability and convenience for the user.
outputs.L5:
**The Value of Seeing Each Thing as Separate**

The world is full of connections, but it is also important to recognize what makes each thing separate. Each person has a unique story, each idea has its own purpose, and each moment carries its own meaning. When we take the time to notice these differences, we understand life more clearly.

The ability to separate one thought from another helps us make better decisions. It allows us to focus, compare, and choose wisely. In the same way, respecting the separate qualities of each individual helps build stronger relationships. We do not all need to be the same to belong together.

Each part of life has its place. The separate pieces may seem small on their own, but together they create something complete. By appreciating each separate element, we learn to value both individuality and unity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style summary for an invention involving a dual-compartment spray bottle that dispenses two liquids such as bleach and an activator while minimizing residual mixed composition in the dispensing mechanism.
counterfactuals.output:
A dual-compartment spray dispensing system is provided for separately storing and selectively dispensing two liquid compositions, such as a bleach-containing composition and an activator composition, in a combined spray while reducing retention of mixed liquid within the dispensing mechanism. The system includes a container body having a first reservoir for containing a first liquid and a second reservoir for containing a second liquid, the reservoirs being fluidly isolated from one another during storage. A spray head is coupled to the container body and includes separate intake passages communicating respectively with the first and second reservoirs.

In one aspect, the spray head includes first and second liquid flow paths that remain substantially separated until the liquids reach a mixing region located at or proximate to an outlet or nozzle of the dispenser. The mixing region may be configured to combine the liquids immediately prior to discharge, thereby limiting the volume of the dispenser in which a mixed composition is present after actuation. The nozzle may generate a spray, stream, foam, or other discharge pattern suitable for applying the combined composition to a surface.

In another aspect, the dispenser includes a pump or trigger mechanism configured to draw the two liquids from the respective reservoirs in predetermined proportions. The flow ratio may be controlled by passage dimensions, valve structures, pump chamber volumes, restrictors, dip tubes, or combinations thereof. The first and second liquids may be dispensed simultaneously through separate channels and mixed only at the point of spray formation.

The dispensing mechanism may further include features that minimize residual mixed composition, including a reduced-volume mixing chamber, a self-draining outlet region, check valves preventing backflow into upstream passages, air purge passages, resilient return structures, or geometries configured to expel substantially all mixed liquid during each dispensing stroke. In some embodiments, any retained mixed liquid is confined to a small terminal portion of the nozzle assembly, thereby reducing degradation, gas generation, clogging, corrosion, loss of efficacy, or undesirable reaction between the stored liquids.

The first liquid may comprise an oxidizing agent, such as sodium hypochlorite bleach, and the second liquid may comprise an activator, catalyst, surfactant, fragrance, pH-adjusting agent, peroxide component, or other reactive or performance-enhancing composition. By maintaining the liquids in separate compartments until dispensing, the system improves shelf stability while enabling formation of an active cleaning, disinfecting, whitening, or treating composition at the time of use.

The invention therefore provides a convenient spray bottle capable of co-dispensing chemically distinct liquids in a controlled ratio while minimizing residual mixed composition within the spray head after dispensing. This configuration may reduce unwanted reaction during storage and between uses, improve product stability, and extend the useful life and reliability of the dispenser.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in the language of a patent application, a fluid dispensing device that uses separate dip tubes, pumps, and delivery tubes to keep two liquid components separate until they reach the spray nozzle.
counterfactuals.output:
A fluid dispensing device is provided for separately storing, transporting, and dispensing first and second liquid components such that the components remain isolated from one another until discharge at or adjacent a spray nozzle.

In one embodiment, the device comprises a container assembly defining a first reservoir configured to contain a first liquid component and a second reservoir configured to contain a second liquid component. The first and second reservoirs may be formed as separate chambers within a common container body, as separate containers coupled to a common dispensing head, or as replaceable cartridges received in a housing.

A dispensing head is operatively coupled to the container assembly. The dispensing head includes a first pump in fluid communication with the first reservoir and a second pump in fluid communication with the second reservoir. The first pump and the second pump are preferably mechanically actuated by a common actuator, trigger, button, lever, or motorized drive so that the first and second liquid components are dispensed in a predetermined ratio. In alternative embodiments, the pumps may be independently actuated or may have different stroke volumes to provide a selected mixing ratio.

A first dip tube extends from an inlet of the first pump into the first reservoir, and a second dip tube extends from an inlet of the second pump into the second reservoir. The first dip tube is isolated from the second dip tube so that liquid drawn from the first reservoir is not exposed to liquid drawn from the second reservoir. The first pump includes a first pump chamber and associated inlet and outlet valve structures configured to draw the first liquid component through the first dip tube and expel the first liquid component through a first outlet. The second pump includes a second pump chamber and associated inlet and outlet valve structures configured to draw the second liquid component through the second dip tube and expel the second liquid component through a second outlet.

A first delivery tube extends from the first pump outlet toward a spray nozzle, and a second delivery tube extends from the second pump outlet toward the spray nozzle. The first delivery tube and the second delivery tube define separate and non-communicating flow paths along substantially their entire lengths. The delivery tubes may be formed as discrete tubes, as separate lumens within a multi-lumen conduit, or as molded channels within the dispensing head. Seals, partitions, valve seats, gaskets, or integrally formed walls may be provided to prevent intermixing of the first and second liquid components upstream of the nozzle.

The spray nozzle is arranged to receive the first liquid component from the first delivery tube and the second liquid component from the second delivery tube. In one embodiment, the nozzle includes separate first and second nozzle inlets communicating respectively with the first and second delivery tubes. The nozzle may maintain the components in separate streams until the streams exit respective discharge openings, whereupon the streams intersect, impinge, atomize, or otherwise combine externally of the nozzle. In another embodiment, the nozzle includes a short mixing region located immediately upstream of one or more discharge orifices, such that the first and second liquid components first contact one another only within the nozzle or at a region directly adjacent the discharge orifice.

The device may be configured so that the first liquid component and the second liquid component are chemically reactive, unstable when premixed, or otherwise preferably maintained separately prior to use. By providing separate dip tubes, separate pumps, and separate delivery tubes, premature reaction, degradation, clogging, crystallization, viscosity change, gas formation, or loss of active ingredient may be reduced or avoided.

In use, actuation of the common actuator causes the first pump to draw the first liquid component from the first reservoir through the first dip tube and simultaneously causes the second pump to draw the second liquid component from the second reservoir through the second dip tube. Continued actuation expels the first liquid component through the first delivery tube and expels the second liquid component through the second delivery tube. The two components remain fluidically separated until reaching the spray nozzle, where they are combined at, within, or immediately downstream of the nozzle and discharged as a spray, mist, foam, stream, or other dispensed pattern.

The device may further comprise one or more check valves positioned in the first and second flow paths to prevent backflow of one component into the flow path of the other component. The nozzle may also include anti-drip features, shutoff valves, or removable and cleanable nozzle elements. The first and second pumps may be piston pumps, diaphragm pumps, bellows pumps, peristaltic pumps, gear pumps, or other positive displacement pumps suitable for delivering metered quantities of fluid. The pumps may be selected to dispense equal or unequal volumes per actuation, thereby controlling the ratio of the first and second components at the point of dispensing.

Accordingly, the dispensing device provides isolated storage and conveyance of multiple liquid components through dedicated dip tubes, pump chambers, and delivery passages, with combination of the components occurring only at the nozzle region to enable on-demand mixing immediately prior to or during discharge.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical abstract for a cleaning product sprayer with first and second compartments, explaining embodiments with dual pumps as well as alternatives using a single pump or delivery tube.
counterfactuals.output:
A cleaning product sprayer includes a container having first and second compartments configured to separately store respective first and second cleaning compositions, and a dispensing head coupled to the container for selectively dispensing the compositions. In some embodiments, the dispensing head includes first and second pumps in fluid communication with the first and second compartments, respectively, such that actuation of a trigger or other actuator draws the first composition from the first compartment through a first fluid path and the second composition from the second compartment through a second fluid path. The compositions may be discharged through separate outlets, a common outlet, or a mixing chamber upstream of an outlet to provide simultaneous, sequential, or selectable dispensing.

In other embodiments, the sprayer employs a single pump fluidly connectable to both compartments through one or more valves, selectors, manifolds, or flow-control elements. The single pump may draw from either compartment independently, from both compartments concurrently, or from the compartments in a selected ratio. The dispensing head may include a user-operable selector for choosing the first composition, the second composition, a mixed output, or an off condition.

Alternative embodiments include a delivery tube arrangement in which one or more dip tubes, conduits, or transfer passages extend into the first and second compartments and cooperate with a pump, valve, venturi, siphon, or pressure-driven dispensing mechanism to deliver the stored compositions to an outlet. The compartments may be formed integrally within a common bottle or provided as separate reservoirs received by a common sprayer body. The separated storage of the compositions enables incompatible or reactive cleaning ingredients to be maintained apart prior to use while permitting convenient dispensing from a single handheld sprayer.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for a bottle that dispenses different liquids from separate compartments and delays mixing to avoid leftover mixed chemicals in the pump or tubing.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a multi-compartment dispensing bottle designed to store two or more liquids separately and mix them only at or near the time of use. Each liquid is held in its own compartment and delivered through separate flow paths, such as individual tubes or channels, toward a common outlet.

A key feature is that the system delays or prevents premature mixing inside the pump, nozzle, or tubing. Instead of allowing the liquids to combine and remain trapped in shared internal passages after dispensing, the design keeps them separated until they exit the bottle or reach a final mixing area close to the discharge point. This reduces or eliminates leftover mixed chemicals inside the dispenser.

The benefit is especially useful for products whose ingredients react, degrade, harden, clog, lose effectiveness, or create unwanted residue after mixing. By keeping the components apart during storage and most of the dispensing process, the bottle improves shelf life, reduces clogging and contamination, and allows the user to dispense freshly combined liquids in controlled proportions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent disclosure paragraph about a dual-liquid dispensing spray device designed to reduce or eliminate the need for priming by preventing residual mixed composition.
counterfactuals.output: A dual-liquid dispensing spray device includes first and second reservoirs containing respective liquid components, separate pump chambers and delivery conduits for the components, and a spray head configured to combine the components only at or immediately upstream of a discharge orifice. The device includes one-way valves, isolated flow paths, and/or a suck-back or purge feature arranged to prevent mixed composition from remaining in shared passages after actuation. Upon release of the actuator, residual unmixed liquids are retained in their respective conduits while any mixed composition at the mixing region is discharged, withdrawn, or isolated from the supply paths. By minimizing the volume in which the components coexist and preventing backflow of mixed material into the device, the dispenser reduces curing, clogging, or degradation between uses and thereby reduces or eliminates the need for priming before subsequent spraying.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
